Subtracting the average dose from `dose` makes the intercept the [log-odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-logodds) of death at the average dose.
It also moves the [likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-lik) surface closer to the origin, which makes the surface easier to plot.

```{r}
#| results: asis
beetles_glm_grouped_centered <- beetles |>
  glm(
    formula = cbind(died, survived) ~ dose_c,
    family = "binomial"
  )

beetles_glm_ungrouped_centered <- beetles_long |>
  mutate(died = outcome) |>
  glm(
    formula = died ~ dose_c,
    family = "binomial"
  )

equatiomatic::extract_eq(beetles_glm_ungrouped_centered)
```

:::{#tbl-beetles-model-centered}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
beetles_glm_grouped_centered |>
  parameters::parameters() |>
  parameters::print_md()
```

Fitted [logistic regression model](#def-logistic-regression) for `beetles` data, with `dose` centered
